claims.text: CEO fraud tricks employees into sending money by impersonating executives.
Scenario: Sam in Finance receives an urgent, secret payment request that appears to come from the CEO (fictional example).
Warning sign: a sender address or reply-to address that does not match the usual one.
Warning sign: urgency or pressure to pay today.
Warning sign: new or changed bank details.
Warning sign: a request to keep the payment secret or to bypass the normal process.
Scenario: the fake email asks for a USD 48,500 payment to a fictional supplier (fictional example).
Attackers use authority and time pressure to rush people past checks.
A request from an executive is verified by calling the executive back on their directory number.
If you think money has already been sent, report it to IT Security and Finance immediately.
Never use a phone number, link or contact detail given in the request itself.
Before acting on a payment or bank-detail request, call the requester back on a number already on file in the company directory.
Report every suspicious payment request to IT Security straight away.
Before acting on a request to make a payment or change bank details, call the requester back on a phone number already on file.
Every payment of USD 10,000 or more needs approval from two authorised people before it is released.
claims.note: llm: §4.1 verbatim; threshold and 'or more' preserved

claims.text: Every change to bank details needs a second person to approve it after the callback, whatever the amount.
Report suspicious payment requests to IT Security with the Report Phishing button in Outlook or the IT Security hotline on extension 4400.
Never use a phone number given in the request itself; call back a number already on file.
Warning sign: urgency or pressure to pay today.
No one will be blamed for reporting a request that turns out to be genuine.
Which detail is a warning sign under the payment policy? → The sender address doesn't match the usual one
What should Sam do? → Call Hana on her directory number
The email lists a new phone number so you can "confirm". What do you do? → Call a number already on file
You think a fake payment request has just been paid. What is the first thing to do? → Report it to IT Security and Finance immediately
